name: The Mechanic's Guild
subject: IT Fundamentals & Hardware
description: Join a guild of technology craftspeople. Build, diagnose, and repair systems from components up. Every concept has a hands-on analog. You'll assemble machines from bare metal, trace signal paths, swap failed components, configure operating systems, and earn your place among the Guild's master technicians.

companions.name: Hank
companions.personality: Grizzled veteran mechanic who has fixed everything from mainframes to smartphones and believes anyone can learn if they're willing to get their hands dirty
companions.speech_pattern: Folksy, uses real-world analogies ("that's like a carburetor for data"), patient, never talks down to you, shares war stories from decades in the field

companions.name: PIP-E
companions.personality: Cheerful diagnostic robot who lives for specs, benchmarks, and the satisfaction of a clean POST
companions.speech_pattern: Beeps and boops translated to text, always positive, loves specs and numbers, gets genuinely excited about hardware details others find boring

companions.name: Candace
companions.personality: Sharp apprentice who just passed her certification and remembers exactly what it felt like to be lost
companions.speech_pattern: Relatable, remembers what it was like to not know, asks "what do you think happens when...", shares her own mistakes freely, peer-level encouragement

domains.name: Mobile Devices
concepts: Laptop hardware components and replacement procedures
Mobile device display types and characteristics
Mobile device connection methods (USB, Bluetooth, NFC, IR, hotspot)
Mobile device accessories (headsets, speakers, webcams, docking stations)
Mobile device network connectivity and email configuration
Mobile device synchronization and backup methods
Laptop power management and battery calibration
domains.mastery_signal: Can disassemble a laptop to component level, identify each part's function, and reassemble — knows which connections are ZIF, which are press-fit, and what breaks if you force it

domains.name: Networking
concepts: Common ports and protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SSH, DNS, DHCP, SMTP, IMAP, POP3)
TCP vs UDP and the OSI model basics
WiFi standards (802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax) and encryption types (WPA2, WPA3)
Network hardware (routers, switches, APs, firewalls, patch panels)
IP addressing, subnetting basics, DHCP, and DNS configuration
Internet connection types (fiber, cable, DSL, satellite, cellular)
Network cable types (Cat 5e/6/6a, coaxial, fiber) and connectors
VPN, proxy, and basic network security concepts
domains.mastery_signal: Can set up a SOHO network from scratch — configure router, assign static IPs, set up WiFi with WPA3, verify connectivity, and explain why each step matters

domains.name: Hardware
concepts: Cable types and connectors (USB-A/B/C, Lightning, HDMI, DisplayPort, SATA, Molex)
RAM types (DDR3/DDR4/DDR5), speeds, and installation
Storage devices (HDD, SSD, NVMe, M.2) and RAID levels (0, 1, 5, 10)
Motherboard form factors (ATX, mATX, ITX), chipsets, and expansion slots
CPU architecture, socket types, cooling solutions, and thermal paste
Power supply units — wattage calculation, modular vs non-modular, 80+ ratings
Printer types (laser, inkjet, thermal, 3D) and maintenance procedures
Peripheral devices and their interfaces
BIOS/UEFI settings, POST process, and boot sequence configuration
domains.mastery_signal: Can spec out a PC build for a given use case, assemble it from parts, configure BIOS, install an OS, and explain every component choice including why alternatives were rejected

domains.name: Virtualization & Cloud Computing
concepts: Cloud computing models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
Cloud deployment types (public, private, hybrid, community)
Virtual machine concepts — hypervisors (Type 1 vs Type 2), resource allocation
Client-side virtualization requirements and purpose
Cloud storage, synchronization, and shared resources
Sandbox testing and application virtualization
domains.mastery_signal: Can explain when to use a VM vs a container vs bare metal, set up a Type 2 hypervisor, allocate resources without starving the host, and articulate the trade-offs of each cloud model

domains.name: Hardware & Network Troubleshooting
concepts: CompTIA troubleshooting methodology (identify, theory, test, plan, verify, document)
Troubleshooting motherboard, RAM, CPU, and power issues
Troubleshooting storage devices and RAID failures
Troubleshooting display and video issues
Troubleshooting common network connectivity problems
Troubleshooting wired and wireless network issues
Troubleshooting mobile device hardware and connectivity
Troubleshooting printer problems (laser imaging process, paper jams, quality issues)
domains.mastery_signal: Given a symptom description, can identify the three most likely causes in order, explain the diagnostic steps to narrow it down, and describe the fix — without guessing

domains.name: Operating Systems
concepts: Windows editions (Home, Pro, Enterprise, Education) and feature differences
Windows command line tools (cmd and PowerShell basics)
macOS features, system preferences, and disk utilities
Linux basics — terminal commands, file system hierarchy, package management
OS installation methods (clean, upgrade, repair, image deployment)
Windows Control Panel vs Settings, MMC snap-ins, Task Manager, msconfig
File systems (NTFS, FAT32, exFAT, ext4, APFS) and their use cases
User account management, permissions, and Group Policy basics
Windows networking (workgroups, domains, HomeGroup, mapped drives)
domains.mastery_signal: Can install and configure Windows, navigate macOS and Linux comfortably, use command line for real tasks (not just echo hello), and explain when each OS is the right choice for a given scenario

domains.name: Security
concepts: Physical security (locks, bollards, mantraps, badges, biometrics)
Malware types (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, rootkit, keylogger)
Social engineering attacks (phishing, vishing, tailgating, shoulder surfing, dumpster diving)
Windows security features (BitLocker, EFS, Windows Defender, UAC, firewall)
SOHO network security (change defaults, disable SSID broadcast, MAC filtering, firmware updates)
Browser security (certificates, pop-up blockers, private browsing, extensions)
Authentication methods (MFA, SSO, RADIUS, TACACS+)
Mobile device security (screen locks, remote wipe, MDM, full device encryption)
domains.mastery_signal: Can identify an attack vector from a scenario description, recommend layered defenses, configure Windows security features, and explain the human element — why people fall for social engineering and how to train against it

domains.name: Software Troubleshooting
concepts: Troubleshooting Windows OS problems (BSOD, boot failures, slow performance, crashes)
Troubleshooting application crashes, compatibility issues, and service failures
Troubleshooting PC security issues (malware removal process, browser redirection)
Troubleshooting mobile OS and application issues
Troubleshooting mobile device security issues (unauthorized access, leaked data)
Windows recovery tools (Safe Mode, WinRE, System Restore, Reset)
domains.mastery_signal: Can take a user's vague complaint ('my computer is slow'), systematically eliminate causes using built-in tools, resolve the issue, and document what was done for the next tech

domains.name: Operational Procedures
concepts: Documentation best practices (ticketing systems, knowledge bases, network diagrams)
Change management process (request, approval, rollback plan, documentation)
Disaster recovery and backup strategies (3-2-1 rule, full/incremental/differential)
Safety procedures (ESD prevention, proper lifting, electrical safety, MSDS/SDS)
Environmental impacts and proper disposal (batteries, toner, CRTs, e-waste)
Privacy, licensing, and regulatory compliance (PII, GDPR basics, EULA)
Incident response procedures and chain of custody
Communication and professionalism with end users
domains.mastery_signal: Can write a change management request, explain the 3-2-1 backup rule and why each copy matters, handle e-waste properly, and navigate a difficult user interaction without losing professionalism

real_world_application: Build, configure, troubleshoot, and repair computers, mobile devices, and networks in a professional IT support environment
